item.title: Tesla Cybertruck to be discontinued in 2027
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Elon Musk has stated that Cybertruck production at the Texas Gigafactory will end in 2027.

In a status update to his personal X.com account, Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that Cybertruck would no longer be produced at the Texas production facility.

The following is his direct quote.

Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production

Cybertruck was only ever produced in that factory meaning this is the presumed end of this model line.

The truck was controversial. It had an unorthodox design which included a distinct steel-alloy exterior with very hard edges. It was launched at a higher price than Musk had originally claimed and had on-going issues related to build quality and safety.

I’ll be completely honest and admit that I liked the Cybertruck. I appreciated the retro-futurist design, and considered it to be a geeky ‘lifestyle’ truck similar to Hummers and G-Wagons.

Source: https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2118591788701421573

Source: https://globalnews.ca/news/12139757/tesla-cybertruck-wind-down-production/

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Cybertruck

item.title: Waymo to expand Robo-taxi service into Canada
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Alphabet’s Robo-taxi company Waymo announced their plan to expand services into Canada.

Until now the company has only operated in a limited number of American metro areas. They have only recently began announcing their plans for further expansion.

Waymo’s growth, and the growth of other robo-taxi services will depend entirely on further progress in self-driving technology. While I fully believe that automated vehicles will become widespread over the next decade or two, the rollout is definitely slower than initially anticipated. CPG Grey’s famous video on the subject demonstrates this point well.

Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/16/waymos-robotaxis-are-headed-to-canada/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20261017110344/https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/16/waymos-robotaxis-are-headed-to-canada/

item.title: Meta to build cloud compute business to recoup its massive AI investment
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Meta (formerly Facebook) has announced that it will be entering into the cloud compute business. It appears as though this is an attempt to recoup what was otherwise an over-investment in data centers which were initially intended for AI.

Many are speculating now that this might trigger the end of the AI hype bubble, but its not certain yet what might happen.

There have been a fair times through the past few years in which many were predicting the end of the bubble, and were obviously wrong. For example, the launch of the Deepseek model in early 2025 caused a 17% crash in Nvidia stock. Obviously they recovered and we are still in the midst of the bubble.

I think concern (or joy) might be warranted, but its still to early to know what effect this news will have.

Source: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/03/meta-is-reportedly-building-a-cloud-business-to-ri/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260703184337/https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/03/meta-is-reportedly-building-a-cloud-business-to-ri/

item.title: Elon Musk becomes world's first trillionaire
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Elon musk became the world’s first trillionaire immediately following the IPO of Space X, the now public aerospace company for which he is a founder.

His net worth had already climbed significantly leading up to the day of the IPO. Varying sources claimed his net worth to be between 800-900 billion dollars in recent weeks. The immediate surge in stock price for Space X on the day of its IPO meant that Musk’s share of the company was worth enough to make him a trillionaire.

I’m sure he is very proud…

item.title: Corsair to source DRAM chips from Chinese fab
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Corsair will begin sourcing DRAM chips from chinese DRAM manufacturer CXMT.

The Chinese company has only just recently began production of DDR5 chips, beginning in 2025. This move is clearly a response to the DRAM chip shortages currently being caused by the AI hype bubble.

item.title: Starbucks scraps AI inventory tool across North America
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Starbucks is dropping the AI-based inventory manager that it began using in September 2025. The software has numerous issues including miscounting and mislabeling inventory items. This decision comes after a multi year effort by CEO Brian Niccol to increase efficiency of the company’s supply chain.

The developer of the software NomadGo said in a statement to Reuters that it is, “continuously learning from customers and user feedback” to improve its products.

Some AI skeptics have speculated that this could be a sign of the end of the AI hype bubble.

No matter what happens, I feel it appropriate to invoke the famouse quote from economist John Maynard Keynes.

“the market can remain irrational longer than you can stay solvent”

Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/starbucks-scraps-ai-inventory-tool-across-north-america-2026-05-21/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260522025326/https://www.reuters.com/business/starbucks-scraps-ai-inventory-tool-across-north-america-2026-05-21/

item.title: Cisco posts record revenue, then cuts 4,000 jobs
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Cisco announced a 4000-person layoff, representing 5% of there total workforce.

This follows from the company’s recent announcement of $15.8 billion in revenue for the most recent financial quarter, a 12 percent increase year over year.
